description: This source file contains the implementation of the interpretive instruction engine for Luminary, including its core loop, address decoding, and execution model. It defines entry points, resume routines, main dispatching functions, address handling mechanisms, store operations, and constants used by interpretive programs.

methods.name: INTPRET
methods.description: Entry point for the interpretive instruction engine, initializes the interpreter state and begins execution.

methods.name: INTRSM
methods.description: Routine to resume interpretive jobs after suspension, managing context switching.

methods.name: DANZIG
methods.description: Main interpretive dispatcher loop that handles opcode execution, job switching, and program flow control.

methods.name: NEWOPS
methods.description: Fetches the next interpretive opcode pair and prepares execution.

methods.name: ADDRESS
methods.description: Translates interpretive instructions into memory addresses, handling various addressing modes.

methods.name: DIRADRES
methods.description: Handles direct addressing resolution based on address thresholds and bank switching rules.

methods.name: EBANK
methods.description: Sets the erasable bank for subsequent memory operations.

methods.name: FBANK
methods.description: Sets the fixed bank for fixed memory addressing.

methods.name: PUSHUP
methods.description: Retrieves operands from the pushdown list when explicit addresses are not given.

methods.name: STORJUMP
methods.description: Handles jump-based store operations, including subroutine calls in interpretive programs.

methods.name: DOSTORE
methods.description: Dispatches store commands, routing interpretive output as per opcode.

methods.name: CALL
methods.description: Sets up return points and invokes subroutines within interpretive execution.

methods.name: RTB
methods.description: Return to basic language or control code at specified address.

methods.name: INDEX
methods.description: Processes indexed address calculations using interpretive index registers.
